title: Nightly jobs and the day work around them
summary: Williams tells of playing most nights, including at the Marcelloan on Charters Street, the Fifth Ward Athletic Club and Shadowland, with trumpeters Rickard Lexkin and Herman Franklin.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah, he played all over there. What would you do during the day when you

played music back in those times? I used to like the wood. Loved the wood. Drive, truck, drive, truck, and sometimes I'd get on a job and play every night. I played at the Marcelloan on Charter Street until they come in with a big doobie. They come in with a big doobie. I don't know that place. Charters and what? It was on Charters between St. Phillip. Charters between St. Phillip and Domaine. On that side of the
area. I know that neighborhood but I... It was in my salon. Near the ice house there?

Near the ice house, yeah. And then I used to play at the Fifth Ward Athletic Club. To play there every night. Is that near Patonis? In Patonis Place. That's Patonis Place. Yeah, I used to play there every night. I was working there with Rick High, Rick High Lexkin. And the trumpet player is dead and gone now. I can't think about him. He was in the local. Well, Rickard was playing bass then or trumpet? Rickard was playing trumpet. And you had two trumpets, huh?
When? When... Well, you said you had another trumpet who was in the local. You can't think of his name. Well... A different time.

That was a different time. He was at the Shadowland out in Gentilly. I can't think of his name. That was... Who was George Green who got all that names down in the book. Oh yeah. You know? Uh huh. He was... This guy's cat was on the board too. A little bit of short to talk. He used to have a... On the bulldozer. Used to do a lot of landscaping in the day time. I can't think of his name. I had to get amongst some of the boys that... Franklin. Herman Franklin. Oh yeah, I know him.
Oh yeah. Yeah, we played down at the Rendellview with him a long time.
